statusDetail: All 58 atomic checks were judged across the redirected home/listing, actor index, content detail, and HTTP failure archetypes.

page.framework: Server-rendered PHP-style MPA with jQuery/Layui/Bootstrap-era assets
page.notes: The requested host redirects to yasyadong02.tv. The site is an adult media catalogue; representative content was inspected only as needed for quality evidence.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Raw CSS analysis found no color-scheme declaration or prefers-color-scheme rule; computed color-scheme was normal while the UI remained black.
No active animations were observed on the actors surface, including under reduced-motion emulation; there was no auto-advance to suppress.
Static analysis found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors handling; Lighthouse measured examples at 3.65:1 and 3.98:1, below 4.5:1.
Static HTML/CSS contained no view-transition-name, @view-transition, or View Transition API usage across the MPA listing/detail templates.
No parallax, scrollytelling, scroll reveal, or other scroll-linked animation was present, so there is no scroll handler to replace.
checkOutcomes.reason: No parallax, scrollytelling, scroll reveal, or other scroll-linked animation was present, so there is no scroll handler to replace.

checkOutcomes.evidence: CSS exposes horizontally scrolling mobile rails but static analysis found no scroll-snap or intentional overscroll behavior for those rails.
DOM/CSS evidence shows a fixed 151px header and no scroll-state container query or progress/shrink behavior.
The inspected primary surfaces use a centered modal, not an anchor-attached tooltip, popover, or menu requiring anchor positioning.
checkOutcomes.reason: The inspected primary surfaces use a centered modal, not an anchor-attached tooltip, popover, or menu requiring anchor positioning.

checkOutcomes.method: Desktop screenshot and DOM state inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Active navigation/filter states use a clear red highlight, and the notice modal visually contains the current focus.
The initial desktop capture shows a modal centered over the listing before any user interaction.
DOM/CSS shows .layui-layer custom overlay chrome while the page contains zero dialog and popover elements.
The desktop capture gives the top several rows to affiliate banners, a fixed side rail, tabs, and an overlay before the content grid.
Actors and detail templates at 390x844 had viewport metadata, 390px content width, and 0px horizontal overflow.
The stylesheet has many viewport media queries but no @container/container-type rules, although cards and rails are reused at different widths.
The focus probe found the search input and buttons with outline-style none; several controls also measured 20-40px in one dimension.
The first desktop viewport is dominated by affiliate banners and the notice modal before the content list.
The server-rendered listing exposes real detail links, and the representative detail response contains a titled h1 and native video element.
A representative nonexistent route returns HTTP 404 with only nginx “404 Not Found” text and no navigation, search, or recovery action.
Lighthouse measured LCP 5.3s and CLS 0.601; the corroborating trace measured LCP 2.31s under a different run, showing network-sensitive loading.
Lighthouse measured CLS 0.601 and flagged unsized images; raw analysis found all 157 img elements lacked both width and height attributes.
The trace found three modest long tasks, longest 76ms, with total blocking time 47ms; Lighthouse TBT was 60ms.
HAR recorded 162 requests, 6.11MB transferred, 16 stylesheets and at least ten parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheet candidates.
HAR shows 35 scripts, 16 stylesheets, and a 167KB Google tag script alongside unrelated vendor CSS such as maps and chart/list plugins.
Lighthouse failed image-alt and link-name with multiple logo/navigation images and icon-only links; raw analysis counted 17 images without alt.
Lighthouse reported active controls around 3.98:1 and metadata text at 3.65:1 where 4.5:1 is required.
Lighthouse found headings jumping to h6 and unnamed links; the focus probe found important controls with no visible outline.
Primary card titles and modal body copy are readable at the inspected desktop size, with no clipping observed; contrast failures are recorded separately.
The representative detail markup contains a video but no track element; the focus probe measured controls below 44px. Viewport scaling itself is permitted.
Lighthouse reported no browser console errors on the audited load.
Doctype and charset pass, but Lighthouse flagged unsized images and raw analysis found 157/157 without explicit dimensions.
Raw HTML loads disable-devtool@latest with disable-select and disable-copy, an obstructive behavior that also adds supply-chain risk.
The homepage has a descriptive title and meta description; actors and detail templates also use route-specific titles.
Lighthouse failed crawlable-anchors and link-name; raw inspection counted 11 empty/hash links, while viewport and robots signals passed.

checkOutcomes.method: HTTP chain, canonical, robots, and sitemap inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The requested host redirects successfully to yasyadong02.tv; the final page has a matching canonical, robots allows indexing, and the sitemap lists final-host routes.
The representative detail response has a visible title/video entity but no JSON-LD, Open Graph, or Twitter Card tags.
The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
HAR attributes 159/162 requests and 6.106MB to third-party origins; tracker evidence found 14 third-party origins including Google Analytics and dtscout.
The page exposes login/account entry, but static analysis found no WebAuthn/PublicKeyCredential/passkey integration; no permission-on-load prompt was observed.
All inspected defensive headers were absent; Lighthouse also found a dtscout third-party cookie and DevTools cookie issues.
Core listings, actor indexes, metadata, links, and detail video markup are present in substantial server-rendered HTML rather than an empty JS shell.
The inspected actors/detail layouts stayed within the viewport, and the centered modal remained bounded in the desktop capture.
This is a streaming content MPA whose core media is intrinsically online; no installable/offline product intent was evident, so PWA availability is not required.
checkOutcomes.reason: This is a streaming content MPA whose core media is intrinsically online; no installable/offline product intent was evident, so PWA availability is not required.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The tested 404 is a bare nginx page with no retry, search, navigation, or explanation.
The document correctly sets lang=ko, but static analysis found no logical properties and about 150 left/right declarations.
Rendered relative times and labels are consistently localised in Korean on the inspected server-rendered templates.
No scheduled events, absolute timestamps, calendars, or cross-time-zone coordination surface was present in the representative templates.
checkOutcomes.reason: No scheduled events, absolute timestamps, calendars, or cross-time-zone coordination surface was present in the representative templates.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The first viewport contains many affiliate/gambling banners before the content, while raw links include numerous external affiliates with empty text and no visible “advertisement” disclosure.

checkOutcomes.method: Form markup and Lighthouse labels audit
checkOutcomes.evidence: The public primary flow uses browse/search rather than required data entry; Lighthouse found exposed form controls labelled, and no premature validation was observed.
Raw analysis found all eight inputs without autocomplete; visible search controls rely on generic English placeholder text.
Login/account actions are present, but no passkey integration or account autofill evidence was found.
HAR records 107 image requests and 5.33MB of image transfer; raw analysis found no srcset or lazy loading and every image lacked intrinsic dimensions.
The initial load makes 162 requests, including 159 third-party requests, 35 scripts, and broad vendor CSS before interaction.
Third parties account for 6.106MB of 6.107MB transferred; 14 third-party origins include trackers and 81 image-host requests.
No developer intent for agent-facing transactions or tools was evident; this emerging capability is reasonably out of scope for this public media catalogue.
checkOutcomes.reason: No developer intent for agent-facing transactions or tools was evident; this emerging capability is reasonably out of scope for this public media catalogue.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No summarisation, generation, or other inference task is part of the observed core browsing/video flow, so built-in AI is not applicable.
checkOutcomes.reason: No summarisation, generation, or other inference task is part of the observed core browsing/video flow, so built-in AI is not applicable.

checkOutcomes.method: Before/after heap summaries around repeated real scrolling
checkOutcomes.evidence: After ten full-page scroll cycles on the actors listing, heap self-size changed from 20,506,356 to 20,609,295 bytes (about 0.5%) and node count from 343,499 to 344,668 (about 0.34%), with no unbounded growth signal.
The interactive actors page used about 20.5MB heap self-size and 997 live DOM elements, proportionate to a long media index.
The repeated-scroll heap comparison remained nearly flat; no growing detached/listener symptom was observable from the summary-level evidence.

principleOutcomes.reason: No developer intent for agent-facing transactions or tools was evident; this emerging capability is reasonably out of scope for this public media catalogue. No summarisation, generation, or other inference task is part of the observed core browsing/video flow, so built-in AI is not applicable.

paths.description: Requested homepage redirect and final listing template; covers initial viewport, navigation, search, ads, modal, metadata, network, performance, privacy, and preferences.
Actor index/listing archetype; covers long responsive listing, layout, real repeated scrolling, and memory.
Representative media detail archetype; covers route-specific metadata, heading, video/media accessibility, and mobile layout.
Representative unknown route; covers HTTP status and user recovery.

findings.summary: Theme is hard-coded dark instead of following the user color preference
findings.evidence: Raw CSS analysis found no color-scheme declaration or prefers-color-scheme rule; computed color-scheme was normal while the UI remained black.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and map surface/text tokens through prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), with both usable light and dark palettes.

findings.summary: The interface does not adapt to high-contrast preferences and already fails minimum contrast
findings.evidence: Static analysis found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors handling; Lighthouse measured examples at 3.65:1 and 3.98:1, below 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Use system colors/forced-color-adjust carefully and raise normal-theme foreground contrast to WCAG thresholds.

findings.summary: Page and state changes swap abruptly
findings.evidence: Static HTML/CSS contained no view-transition-name, @view-transition, or View Transition API usage across the MPA listing/detail templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document View Transitions for listing-to-detail and same-document transitions for filter changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Horizontal recommendation rails lack native snap and overscroll affordances
findings.evidence: CSS exposes horizontally scrolling mobile rails but static analysis found no scroll-snap or intentional overscroll behavior for those rails.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS scroll-snap-type/scroll-snap-align and overscroll behavior for touch-native horizontal rails.

findings.summary: The large fixed header does not respond to scroll state
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS evidence shows a fixed 151px header and no scroll-state container query or progress/shrink behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a scroll-state query or a lightweight declarative shrinking header so content gains space after scrolling.

findings.summary: A notice modal obscures primary content on initial load
findings.evidence: The initial desktop capture shows a modal centered over the listing before any user interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not open non-critical notices on load; place the message inline or in a non-modal disclosure, and preserve a clear dismiss action.

findings.summary: The on-load modal uses a custom div-based layer
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS shows .layui-layer custom overlay chrome while the page contains zero dialog and popover elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native dialog for modal notices, with a labelled heading, focus management, Escape/platform dismissal, and no forced opening for non-critical content.

findings.summary: Ads and fixed chrome dominate the first viewport
findings.evidence: The desktop capture gives the top several rows to affiliate banners, a fixed side rail, tabs, and an overlay before the content grid.
findings.suggestedFix: Move promotional inventory below the primary content, label it, and reduce persistent chrome to the controls needed for browsing.

findings.summary: Reusable cards adapt only through viewport breakpoints
findings.evidence: The stylesheet has many viewport media queries but no @container/container-type rules, although cards and rails are reused at different widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable card/rail wrappers containment and adapt components with size container queries, retaining viewport fallbacks where useful.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is removed on key controls
findings.evidence: The focus probe found the search input and buttons with outline-style none; several controls also measured 20-40px in one dimension.
findings.suggestedFix: Use :focus-visible with a high-contrast outline and keep touch targets at least 44 CSS px without hiding focus.

findings.summary: The primary browsing task is buried beneath ads and an unsolicited notice
findings.evidence: The first desktop viewport is dominated by affiliate banners and the notice modal before the content list.
findings.suggestedFix: Lead with the browse/search purpose and content controls; defer and clearly label promotional material.

findings.summary: The HTTP failure state is a dead-end server page
findings.evidence: A representative nonexistent route returns HTTP 404 with only nginx “404 Not Found” text and no navigation, search, or recovery action.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a branded, lightweight 404 with search, home/back links, clear status, and preserved site navigation.

findings.summary: Mobile load performance and stability miss Core Web Vitals targets
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 5.3s and CLS 0.601; the corroborating trace measured LCP 2.31s under a different run, showing network-sensitive loading.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the true LCP image, reserve layout space, lazy-load below-fold media, and cut the initial request/asset set.

findings.summary: Unsized images produce major layout movement
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured CLS 0.601 and flagged unsized images; raw analysis found all 157 img elements lacked both width and height attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio for every image slot and stable dimensions for ad inventory.

findings.summary: The critical path is broad and image-heavy
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 162 requests, 6.11MB transferred, 16 stylesheets and at least ten parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheet candidates.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate critical CSS, defer non-critical vendor styles/scripts, cache immutable assets, and prioritise only the LCP resource.

findings.summary: The page ships a large generic vendor surface for a simple listing
findings.evidence: HAR shows 35 scripts, 16 stylesheets, and a 167KB Google tag script alongside unrelated vendor CSS such as maps and chart/list plugins.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unused vendor bundles per template, split optional features, and load third parties only after consent or interaction.

findings.summary: Images and icon links lack accessible alternatives
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed image-alt and link-name with multiple logo/navigation images and icon-only links; raw analysis counted 17 images without alt.
findings.suggestedFix: Add meaningful alt text or empty alt for decoration, and accessible names for every icon-only link/control.

findings.summary: Text and active controls fail WCAG contrast
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported active controls around 3.98:1 and metadata text at 3.65:1 where 4.5:1 is required.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken red control backgrounds or increase text weight/size, and raise muted text from #666 on black to a compliant token.

findings.summary: Heading hierarchy and keyboard focus are not reliable
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found headings jumping to h6 and unnamed links; the focus probe found important controls with no visible outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a logical h1-h2-h3 hierarchy, labelled landmarks, and a visible :focus-visible treatment following DOM reading order.

findings.summary: Video lacks captions and some controls are undersized
findings.evidence: The representative detail markup contains a video but no track element; the focus probe measured controls below 44px. Viewport scaling itself is permitted.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide WebVTT captions/transcripts for video and enlarge interactive hit areas while preserving user zoom/reflow.

findings.summary: Images are structurally unsized despite a sound document shell
findings.evidence: Doctype and charset pass, but Lighthouse flagged unsized images and raw analysis found 157/157 without explicit dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Retain the valid document shell and add intrinsic dimensions/aspect ratios to every image component.

findings.summary: The site deliberately disables DevTools, selection, and copying
findings.evidence: Raw HTML loads disable-devtool@latest with disable-select and disable-copy, an obstructive behavior that also adds supply-chain risk.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the DevTools/copy-prevention package and allow standard selection, copying, context menus, and inspection.

findings.summary: Several navigation actions are not crawlable or descriptively named
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed crawlable-anchors and link-name; raw inspection counted 11 empty/hash links, while viewport and robots signals passed.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href destinations for navigation, buttons for actions, and descriptive accessible link text.

findings.summary: Content detail pages expose no structured or share-preview metadata
findings.evidence: The representative detail response has a visible title/video entity but no JSON-LD, Open Graph, or Twitter Card tags.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate VideoObject/BreadcrumbList JSON-LD and Open Graph/Twitter metadata matching visible detail content.

findings.summary: HTTPS is present but baseline security headers are absent
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrictive nonce/hash CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, and a minimal Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Nearly the entire load is third-party and includes active tracking
findings.evidence: HAR attributes 159/162 requests and 6.106MB to third-party origins; tracker evidence found 14 third-party origins including Google Analytics and dtscout.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce third parties, gate analytics/advertising behind explicit consent, proxy or self-host essential assets, and document retention/purpose.

findings.summary: Account entry offers no phishing-resistant authentication signal
findings.evidence: The page exposes login/account entry, but static analysis found no WebAuthn/PublicKeyCredential/passkey integration; no permission-on-load prompt was observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration/sign-in and request browser permissions only from a clearly explained user action.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses and third-party-cookie posture are weak
findings.evidence: All inspected defensive headers were absent; Lighthouse also found a dtscout third-party cookie and DevTools cookie issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS, frame-ancestors, CSP/Trusted Types where applicable, strict referrer/permissions policies, and eliminate third-party cookies.

findings.summary: Unknown routes fall through to an unhelpful server error
findings.evidence: The tested 404 is a bare nginx page with no retry, search, navigation, or explanation.
findings.suggestedFix: Handle not-found and network failure states in the site shell with recovery links and retry affordances.

findings.summary: Language is declared but layout CSS is entirely physical
findings.evidence: The document correctly sets lang=ko, but static analysis found no logical properties and about 150 left/right declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep lang=ko, add dir support, and migrate reusable spacing/positioning to inline/block logical properties.

findings.summary: Promotional links are visually mixed into content without clear ad labelling
findings.evidence: The first viewport contains many affiliate/gambling banners before the content, while raw links include numerous external affiliates with empty text and no visible “advertisement” disclosure.
findings.suggestedFix: Clearly label and separate advertising, remove disguised placements, and keep content/navigation visually distinct from commercial promotions.

findings.summary: Search fields omit autocomplete and clear purpose tokens
findings.evidence: Raw analysis found all eight inputs without autocomplete; visible search controls rely on generic English placeholder text.
findings.suggestedFix: Give search inputs a programmatic label, input purpose, enterkeyhint, and appropriate autocomplete policy; use correct tokens on any account forms.

findings.summary: Account authentication lacks modern assistance and passkeys
findings.evidence: Login/account actions are present, but no passkey integration or account autofill evidence was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Support passkeys and correct sign-in autocomplete tokens; make account commitments, privacy, and reversal controls explicit.

findings.summary: The page ships a large, non-responsive image set
findings.evidence: HAR records 107 image requests and 5.33MB of image transfer; raw analysis found no srcset or lazy loading and every image lacked intrinsic dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP responsive sources, add srcset/sizes, lazy-load below-fold images, and reserve dimensions.

findings.summary: Most network work happens before it can provide user value
findings.evidence: The initial load makes 162 requests, including 159 third-party requests, 35 scripts, and broad vendor CSS before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer optional content/third parties until visible or requested, remove unused bundles, and prioritise background fetches below user work.

findings.summary: Third-party and promotional media dominate the transfer budget
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 6.106MB of 6.107MB transferred; 14 third-party origins include trackers and 81 image-host requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a per-template byte/origin budget, remove low-value partners, defer media, and self-host/cache essential assets.

taskList.title: Cut initial ads, third parties, and image weight
Reserve image and ad dimensions to eliminate CLS
Remove the on-load custom modal or rebuild it as a native dialog
Restore accessible names, contrast, focus, hierarchy, and captions
Deploy a defensive header and privacy baseline
Remove DevTools/copy prevention and reduce generic vendor code
Replace bare failure pages with recoverable site states
Make navigation and rich detail metadata crawler-friendly
Separate and label advertising; improve account/input trust
